messages.author: 4ff71d47ebc3c595
messages.subject: Re: Proposal II for Google Summer Code 2013 with R
parts:
One needs to know that R is not the first choice for doing Statistics in some region of the World. Not only because it's difficult to learn but Statisticians are often blinded by CSPRO or ACCESS (for data entry) and STATA (for analysis). They, often, think that R is for Medicine or BioStatistics. Introducing this option for R would be a great advertisement and why not attracting people doing all the works with R?
Further, R has many capabilities than these software may find difficult to do:
a) I have in mind: regular expressions. I don't think that with CSPRO, one can easily control if the email entered is a valid or if a number is a correct phone number,...
b) It's even worse with ACCESS. With VBA, in order to manipulate observations, one must define what they call recordset (~like a subset of dataframe in R) so one must declare ugly code which looks like the following:
     Dim area_client_source As recordset
     Set mybase = DBEngine.Workspaces(0).Databases(0)
     mysql = "YOUR SQL CODE HERE...."
     Set area_client_source = mybase.OpenRecordset(mysql, dbOpenDynaset)

     Or with R, we just need to identify each cells of our user interface by something like this "area_client_source[n,names(area_client_source)==k];...."
and so one

I agree R has some fantastic data entry methods, (though a reasonable
SQL engine is quite nice for slice-and-dice as well) but I'm still not
clear on what exactly you want _to do_: package writing, a GUI, etc?

Please don't think I'm trying to drive you away -- your enthusiasm is
most certainly appreciated. I'm just trying to help you refine your
ideas into a project which fits well into the pre-existing R
ecosystem.

The most important question if you're starting a project de novo
(instead of extending something which already exists) is to ask what
hole does it fill. What I'm hearing is that R fills holes in SAS,
Access, etc., but what I'd like to hear is what hole in R you'd like
to fill.

Cheers,
MW
